description: Roman M1 economy mechanics with manual-candidate costs and explicit placeholders for unobserved values.

tickRate.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
tickRate.note: Original clock rate and speed settings are unobserved; 20 ticks per second is an engineering choice.

goods.note: Roman goods named by the occupations and production chains; complete catalog requires decoded content.

tools.note: Tool requirements: builders hammer, diggers shovel, woodcutter axe, stonecutter and miner pick, farmer scythe, fisherman rod, smiths hammer.

terrain.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
terrain.note: Terrain classes and traversal costs are placeholders until decoded landscape types are reconciled.

objects.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
objects.note: Tree regrowth, stone quantity and crop timing are unobserved.

professions.note: Occupation and tool pairing; specialist status follows the manual occupation descriptions.

professions.geologist.tool.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
professions.geologist.tool.note: Geologist tool is not explicit in the manual text.

professions.pioneer.tool.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
professions.pioneer.tool.note: Pioneer tool requirement is not stated in the manual text.

movement.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
movement.note: Movement, slope and occupancy timings are placeholders; the reference remake documents changed movement speed.

movement.searchLimit.note: Bounded routing search is an engineering safety limit.

logistics.groundPileCapacity.note: Craftsmen stop when eight goods lie before the door; storage areas hold six piles of eight.

logistics.carrierCapacity.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
logistics.carrierCapacity.note: Single-good carrier loads match observed sprites but are not yet an admitted observation.

logistics.assignmentInterval.note: Scheduling cadence is an engineering decision and is not original behavior.

logistics.constructionFirst.note: Delivery of goods to building sites has priority over delivery to storage areas.

population.note: Minimum carrier ratio applies to newly added settlers; builder and digger ratios are player controls.

population.values.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
population.values.note: Default ratios and limits are placeholders.

demolition.note: Half of the materials needed for construction become available after demolition.

territory.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
territory.note: Territory radii and pioneer work rate are unobserved.

visibility.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
visibility.note: Vision radii and refresh cadence are placeholders.

survey.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
survey.note: Geologist survey radius, timing and sign lifetime are unobserved.

professions.soldiers.note: Soldier health and strength by rank, melee and pike reach, bow range 7 to 15 and 25 from towers, and one second between blows (1.2 for bows) follow the reference remake; not original observations.

military.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
military.note: Recruitment time, search radius in this engine and defence reach are placeholders; the search radius and tower bow range follow reference constants.

military.wealth.note: Damage scales with ln(gold + start) / (9 ln 2) by number of players, at least full strength on own ground, as the reference computes it; the manual confirms only that gold strengthens soldiers.

religion.note: One wine every 30 seconds for one manna, promotion costs 10, 20, 30, 50, 60, 30 in order with no class more than a rank ahead of another, 8 manna once for a completed large temple and at most 100 priests per large temple follow the reference remake.

religion.interventions.note: Eight Roman interventions and what each does: the Magic Eye lifts fog and needs no priest nearby, Grassland Galore turns desert to grass, Gorgeous Growth speeds grain and grapes, Festering Fear halves enemy damage in your homeland for a short time, Heavenly Presents rains goods, the Midas Touch turns iron into gold, Vanishing Resources halves enemy mine resources, and Conversion wins enemy soldiers over.

religion.interventions.values.note: Manna costs rising by a tenth per use, radii, limits, a 6 second eye, a 300 second growth effect at double speed, 30 seconds of half damage, up to 5 gift piles of up to 8 goods, up to 40 iron, half resources, up to 10 converted soldiers and a 10 tile casting distance follow the reference remake.

thieves.note: Thieves are converted from carriers, look like carriers to opponents until they come too near an enemy soldier, who then pursues them, pilfer goods when ordered with ALT, and are slow while carrying loot home.

thieves.values.note: Health 100 and a 30 tile search for goods on foreign land follow the reference remake. The uncovering distance of 3 and the doubled step time while carrying are placeholders.

buildings.healers-hut.heal.note: The healer calls the most wounded soldier of his player within 20 tiles of the work area to the heal spot and restores full health, one treatment per four seconds; the manual confirms healers return wounded soldiers to health. Soldiers carrying out an order are not called, since the manual has the player send wounded soldiers to the healer.

religion.offerings.note: The small temple transforms wine offerings into manna; promotion needs manna, every promotion costing more than the one before.

religion.priestTicks.note: A new priest every five minutes once a large temple stands; the reference remake uses ten minutes.

objects.vine.note: Vines ripen after nine minutes and are planted on grass beside a height difference of two, with no vine along that slope. Withering after three unharvested minutes is not modelled yet.

buildings.winery.workflow.note: Grapes grow on sloping terrain in the selected work area; the wine-grower needs no tool. The reference work radius is 4.

buildings.small-temple.door.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
buildings.small-temple.door.note: The reference places the small temple door inside its footprint, where it only marks the offering bowl; the engine uses the wine pile as the entrance until the original is observed.

buildings.charcoal-maker.recipe.note: Five boards make one piece of charcoal, usable wherever coal is needed.

military.promotion.note: Promotion affects soldiers recruited afterwards; existing soldiers keep their rank.

buildings.garrison.note: A small tower holds one infantry place and two bowman places; the castle holds five and six.

buildings.barracks.cost-discrepancy.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
buildings.barracks.cost-discrepancy.note: The manual table gives 4 planks and 5 stone; the reference definition gives 5 planks and 4 stone. The manual candidate is used until observed.

buildings.castle.cost.note: Roman wood (planks) and stone columns of the building material table.

buildings.castle.geometry.note: Blocked and protected tiles, door, pile positions and builder spots from the reference remake definition; not yet compared with original building data.

buildings.castle.timing.source: engineering placeholder; not an original value
buildings.castle.timing.note: Levelling, construction and work-cycle durations are unobserved.
